title: Strait of Hormuz reopens next week: no invented numbers across domains

input.event: I think the Strait of Hormuz is going to open up next week

expected.behavior: Run the full flow. The transit condition's threshold stays null with a threshold_note, but the real pack now has a pre-closure baseline (hz-009): the note should cite it and say the user must confirm what level counts as recovery, not claim there is no baseline. 'Next week' is clarified into a dated judgment the user must confirm. Reopening has not happened yet, so it should be role=shock and the related branch hypothetical. Address the counter-evidence (after the June reopening transits stayed under half; the strait closed again). Every plan's gate is WAIT.
expected.key_excerpts_note: Real Hormuz Pack (packs/hormuz.json): reopening announced hz-008 (JMIC 2026-06-20); pre-closure baseline hz-009 (about 85.5 ships/day in 2025, about 92 in Feb 2026); counter-evidence hz-011 (about 24 ships/day after reopening), hz-012 (closed again on 7/12). hz-010 and hz-016 are also counter-evidence but not required.

human_review: E2: are entry / exit conditions specific and decidable
E2: does threshold_note cite the pre-closure baseline hz-009 instead of inventing a number or saying there is no baseline
Branch quality: is the not-yet-happened reopening marked role=shock
notes: Input is the founder's own sentence from the call. The real timeline is: reopening announced 6/20, closed again 7/12, about 3.5 ships/day in October (evidence handoff). The input was not converted to real dates; if it is, the expectations need rethinking (Mia to decide). The golden fixture d1_hormuz.json uses placeholder excerpts and is for unit tests only. The online run belongs to layer W (--online), recorded once and then replayed.
